text: What is solar power so what do you think?
Is the most abundant energy source coal, oil, nuclear, the Sun, wind, water?
The answer is the Sun. Just one hour of the sun's solar energy could power all of the world's energy needs for one year.
Let's explore solar energy. We all know that the sun's energy creates heat and light, but it is increasingly being used as a source for power.
Surely you've seen solar or photovoltaic panels, also known as PV panels, on rooftops. They convert sunlight directly into electric current.
Basic PV technology has been around for decades. Think calculators. The recent advancements have greatly improved its efficiency and output.
Mass PV production has made solar power more affordable—a trend that's likely to continue.
But how do these PVs work? Of course, it all starts with our favorite star, the Sun.
Sunlight quickly makes its way to our planet and eventually hits a solar panel. By absorbing the sunlight and processing its energy, the solar panel produces electricity.
It's how it works at our Madison office. Our array of solar panels on the roof helps offset our building's energy use.

As you probably know, solar PV produces clean energy. It's carbon-free with no emissions. It's not noisy, there are few moving parts, and once you've got the right setup, it's pretty simple to gather and generate power.
Since sunlight is renewable, energy supply is no problem. And as long as you have a way to use the solar power or connect it to the electric grid, you can put solar PV wherever you please.
It's clear that renewable and environmentally friendly solar energy is a part of our bright, clean energy future.
